newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NatSteel spends US$10.2 mln in China deal.
newsitem.headline: NatSteel spends US$10.2 mln in China deal.

text.p: Steel to investments group NatSteel Ltd said on Tuesday it was taking a US$10.2 million stake in China's Wuxi Jinyang Metal Products Co Ltd.

The deal would give NatSteel a 65 percent stake in the prestressed concrete (PC) production company and broaden the Singapore firm's construction product range in China, the company said in a statement.
"Jinyang is a strategic opportunity for NatSteel to expand our products to customers in China," the statement said.
Jinyang was started two years ago with a World Bank loan and produces 20,000 tonnes a year. NatSteel said it wanted to lift output to ithe plant's potential 86,000-tonne capacity.
The deal would also enable NatSteel to tap into "the huge infrastructural potential of the China market", the statement said.

Funding for the deal would be through internal resources and/or bank borrowings. It was not expected to have any material impact on the company's earnings in the current financial year, the statement said.
NatSteel reported pre-tax profits of Singapore $106.5 million on a turnover of S$2.2 billion in its 1996 business year ended December 31.
